extracted.intended_audience: Army commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), unit PA personnel, and other Army staff responsible for public communications and visual information
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs (PA) personnel and commanders on planning, producing, approving, and releasing public communications and visual information, including OPSEC, approval authorities, event support, exhibits, and use of unmanned aerial systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide PA resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide PAOs and PA sections with the resources required to fulfill the Army’s PA mission to include personnel, professional development training, facilities, transportation, equipment, supplies, and financial resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication resources, including access to bandwidth, will be based on commander’s communication requirements, concept of operations, the OE, and comparable industry standards as determined by the APAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPSEC qualification and review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure PAOs are OPSEC level II qualified. The PAO conducts an OPSEC review of all official information before it is released to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of products requiring automatic review include: news releases; web content; teaching, speaking, and writing done by military personnel pertaining to military and national security matters in an unofficial capacity; subjects of significant concern to DoD; and responses to FOIA and Privacy Act requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate and synchronize communication (CCS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate, synchronize, and assess their CCS, plans, campaigns, and engagements; develop command’s communication synchronization process through coordinated PA programs, plans, themes, messages, and products specific to their command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure command-level communication initiatives are aligned with DA themes and messages and commanders are knowledgeable of any differences between inform and influence actions as they apply to mission and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum disclosure, minimum delay for unclassified info
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide unclassified information about the Army and its activities to the public with maximum disclosure and minimum delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not release information that would adversely affect national security, threaten personal safety, or invade the privacy of military members, civilian employees, and their Families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect classified and controlled unclassified information
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect classified information and controlled unclassified information in the interest of national security under AR 380-5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity in releasing unfavorable news
rubrics_metrics.description: Release unfavorable news with the same care and speed as favorable news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct erroneous information
rubrics_metrics.description: Take appropriate action to correct erroneous information about the Army that appears in any medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit staged self-serving publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Not engage in releases, events, or activities staged solely for self-serving or promotional publicity purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support senior commander's PA mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the PA mission of the senior commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and forward support requests appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and approve requests for Army support at the lowest practical command level and forward all requests requiring DA or DoD approval through command channels to the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform CPA of events of national/international interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the CPA of any events that may have national or international interest as soon as details are known prior to the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request augmentation via proper channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Request assistance for PA augmentation by ARNG and U.S. Army Reserve (USAR) when required, submitted through proper ACOM, ASCC, or DRU; CNGB; and ARHQ-FB channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop PA guidance, strategies, and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop proposed PA guidance, strategies, plans, and operations (see DoDI 5405.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate effectiveness of PA activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of PA projects, strategies, plans, and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate official spokespersons
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate spokespersons to release information pertaining to their command; PA is an inherently governmental function requiring that official spokespersons are military, DoD, or Army civilian employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet capability and global monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource and maintain a PA capability to operate on the internet and to monitor the global information environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity for global missions and Army Campaign Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Give adequate publicity throughout the year to the global missions of the Army and the Army Campaign Plan, as directed by the CSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign support requests channeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward requests for support from foreign countries through the proper U.S. Defense Attaché Office to the ATSD (PA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-Service support agreements for tenant/partner support
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop inter-Service support agreements or memoranda of understanding that provide appropriate PA support to tenant units and activities, Army recruiters, ARNG, USAR, and ROTC units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate PA actions with tenant and neighboring activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all actions related to PA areas of responsibility are coordinated with the applicable tenant and neighboring activities and up and down the chain of command; unresolved conflicts referred to higher headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to partisan political and election-year guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Be familiar with and adhere to Army PA policies pertaining to partisan political activities on a military installation and DoD guidance concerning election year activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint and certify UPARs
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint a Unit Public Affairs Representative (UPAR) and ensure certification through the ALMS UPAR and Army OPSEC Training External Official Presence Training certification courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure UPARs operate under the oversight of the higher echelon PAO.

rubrics_metrics.name: External official digital presence compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure any subordinate unit with an external official digital presence complies with the guidance outlined in this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACOM PAO: principal advisor role
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as the principal public communication advisor to the commander; advise commanders regarding functional needs and direct engagements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACOM PAO: develop command-wide communication strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop command-wide communication strategies and plans to include VI planning, functional issuances, and programs in coordination with the commander, subordinate units, and the CPA as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACOM PAO: review and release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as ACOM review and release authority for all information and products intended for public communication on behalf of the commander and command.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACOM PAO: liaison to CPA and planning bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as a functional liaison between the commander and the CPA; provide coordination and representation to CPA planning teams, councils of colonels, and general officer steering committee in support of the CPA, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACOM PAO: align PA products with priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure PA products developed across the command for release through ACOM channels or forwarded to the CPA for Armywide distribution are aligned with ACOM and Army priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop ACOM priorities and messages in coordination with the CPA, as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACOM PAO: functional assessment and assistance visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and coordinate functional assessment of PA operations at the headquarters across subordinate units and conduct regular assistance visits to subordinate units to assess PA programs and determine unit commanders’ needs for support.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACOM PAO: command web content manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as the command web content manager, ensuring command-wide compliance with functional social media and website policies and procedures; responsible for approval of all command content releasable to publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: principal communication advisor (at all levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as the principal communication advisor to the commander, advising commanders on all communication, VI planning, and PA requirements across all mission phases and domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: advise on CCS and implement communication strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide advice and counsel to commanders and appropriate staffs regarding use and employment of the CCS process; plan, develop, and implement all communication strategies for their commander and command.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: designated release and approval authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as the commander’s designated review and approval authority for the release of information to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: supervise PA products
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervise the preparation, production, and distribution of PA communication products.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: advise on audience attitudes and perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise the commander on internal and external audience attitudes and perceptions of policies, programs, and information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: training, visits, and UPAR support
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct regular staff assistance visits to assess subordinate unit PA programs and determine additional support or training requirements; provide training and support to command-designated UPARs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit PA training after action reviews; tactics, techniques, and procedures; and any other lessons learned to APAC for review and input into future PA policy, doctrine, and training development.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: web/social media management and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as the command web and social media content manager, reviewing and releasing official information intended for the internet and command external official presences; conduct routine reviews of subordinate unit publicly accessible websites to ensure compliance with AR 25-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official online content must remain relevant and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO: operational synchronization and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Synchronize PA operations and activities with the operations plan, the communication plan, and other information related capabilities; maintain records in accordance with AR 25-400-2 and DA Pam 25-403.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consult PAO before releasing official information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual who intends to release official information to the public must consult with a PAO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material in its intended release form has a potential security, policy, or propriety violation, it must be submitted for a prepublication review. Retired personnel, former Army employees, and non-active duty members of the RCs will use the security review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective benefit prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation must not selectively benefit or appear to benefit any person, group, or corporation; ACOMs or organizations that provide support to a nonfederal entity must be willing and able to provide equal support to comparable events sponsored by similar nonfederal entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid endorsement rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities will not support any event involving or appearing to involve the promotion, endorsement, or sponsorship of any individual, civilian enterprise, religious or sectarian movement, ideological movement, or political campaign unless it primarily benefits the community at large or the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided include use of shopping malls as community service, airports for aviation events (air shows), and closed events that are cross-section community in nature. Testimonials to individuals generally are not of common interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to veterans service organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating in events sponsored by veterans service organizations may be authorized as long as such participation supports programs oriented to the veteran rather than to sectarian, fraternal, or national origin aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to nonpublic school activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Support may be authorized when participation is clearly educational, patriotic, or in support of Army recruiting programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation limited by nature of sponsoring organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation in events sponsored by organizations with a narrow membership base may be supported only if chiefly benefits the community at large and does not produce special interest benefit to the sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition for restricted-access organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Community outreach support or participation is not authorized for events sponsored by organizations whose constitution, bylaws, membership qualifications, or rituals are withheld from the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army role must be incidental
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation must be incidental to the event; exceptions are patriotic programs, national holiday celebrations, or other appropriate events which must be open to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited use of Army personnel in demeaning event roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel will not be tasked as ushers, bag handlers, guards, escorts at beauty pageants or similar events, messengers, attendants for parking lots, or in similar capacities during public events conducted off military installations or in demeaning or inappropriate capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited use of PA resources
rubrics_metrics.description: PA is a commander’s program and use of PA equipment and personnel will only be for events that support the commander’s approved communication strategy; any use of PA resources for personal social events or any purpose not designed for public release is not authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate recruiting support potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruiting potential will be weighed when evaluating requests for Army participation; applies whether activities are initiated by recruiters, other DA elements, or civilian community elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No support for primarily commercial events
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation is not authorized for events clearly designed or conducted primarily for commercial benefit. Exception: participation may be authorized in direct support of Army recruiting in a shopping center or mall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid competition with commercial entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel, equipment, transportation, or other resources will not be provided to civilian-sponsored activities if commercial resources and services available in the public domain could reasonably provide such support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army support could be provided if documented evidence shows local labor unions and commercial enterprises waived this requirement; all other stipulations in regulation must still be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unauthorized monetary remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: No Army personnel or unit will receive a monetary profit or accept a gratuity or remuneration in any form not permitted by public law or by Army regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for Armed Forces Day/Week
rubrics_metrics.description: Community outreach emphasis during May will be on Armed Forces Day and Armed Forces Week; observances used to demonstrate unity and common purpose of the Armed Forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged acceptance of speaking invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel are encouraged to accept speaking invitations at public events to inform the public of the Army’s mission and its contribution to national security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum effort should be made to satisfy public interest in the Army, either upon request or by invitation, through orientation visits, periodic open houses, briefing and discussion programs, and participation by ARNGUS and USAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider energy and environmental impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy conservation and environmental impact issues will be considered in planning and conducting community outreach activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No association with vote soliciting
rubrics_metrics.description: Community outreach activities cannot be associated with vote soliciting in any political election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See DoDD 1344.10 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No participation in planned confrontational programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Army PA support of, or participation in, community events or programs in which a public confrontation is planned or likely (or where the apparent purpose is to stage controversy) is unauthorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not prevent participation where purpose is fair and equitable exchange of diverse opinions; participation aimed at increasing visibility through direct confrontation is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising endorsement restrictions and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, Army PA support will not officially endorse or appear to endorse fundraising activities for any nonfederal entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ACOM commander or head of organization, after consulting the designated agency ethics official, may authorize endorsement/participation for: Combined Federal Campaign (CFC); emergency/disaster appeals approved by OPM; Army Emergency Relief; fundraising of organizations composed primarily of Army employees for welfare funds if approved; occasional on-post fundraising to assist those in need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited authorization to use facilities/equipment for charitable events
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of an Army organization may provide limited authorization to use Army facilities and equipment and services of Army employees as logistical support of a charitable fundraising event sponsored by a nonfederal entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such support provided only when head of ACOM/organization considers criteria identified in paragraph 3-1b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary private support allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Army members may volunteer in their private capacity to support charities of their choice, encouraged if such efforts do not imply Department of the Army endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requests from other federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Support such as logistics, audiovisual, band, or color guard requested by other Government agencies for an official government event is not considered a community outreach activity and is not subject to the guidance in this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the official nature of the event is questionable, seek guidance from OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Army resources only for events of common interest/benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Army resources will only be used to support events and activities of common interest and benefit to local, state, regional, national, or broadly represented publics; commanders must be willing to give equal consideration and support to comparable events and sponsoring organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational constraints may preclude Army from responding positively to every valid request for support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of local/regional/national publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Local events and publics are restricted to a single community area of responsibility; regional events include participation or interest from more than one state in a section of the U.S.; national events include participation or interest from the U.S. as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA prohibition on psychological operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAOs and their staffs will not initiate or conduct psychological operations and will not permit PA resources to be used to support such activities; violations reported to OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unmanned aerial systems (UAS) use for PA
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult senior commander and review applicable guidance before using UAS to photograph military installations or activities; UAS requests must be submitted through DroneZone for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per FAA, drones must not exceed 55 pounds and the pilot must maintain line of sight with the drone at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate portrayal in visual information (VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: VI will ensure accurate portrayal in situations reflecting Army activities, missions, and uniforms; PAOs will ensure accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No release is required to use images of military personnel serving on active duty or DoD civilians performing their official jobs in PA photos and videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on altering official imagery; permitted modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: No one acting for or on behalf of DA will alter official imagery. Certain modifications are authorized if they do not misrepresent the original subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized modifications include photographic techniques (dodging, burning, color balancing, spotting, adjusting contrast); technical enhancements for cartography/intelligence/medical/etc if they do not misrepresent; masking for security/criminal investigations; cropping/enlarging unless it misrepresents facts; digital conversion/compression; postproduction enhancements for dramatization allowed only if they do not misrepresent or context makes representation apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on releasing imagery of wounded, deceased, or medically treated personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: When releasing VI of U.S. and allied forces personnel killed, wounded, hospitalized, detained, or missing as a result of hostile action, give consideration to rights of individuals and effects on Families and friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official release prohibited (unless permission/notification criteria met) for: photographs/video of recognizable wounded/deceased not identified by name; recognizable wounded identified by name until next of kin notified; surgical/major medical care images identifying patient; photographs showing deceased/wounded in large numbers; photos showing mangled bodies or extreme agony; psychiatric patients; plastic surgery/disfigurement cases; blind or deaf patients; amputees demonstrating prosthetic appliances. Official combat-deceased photos under field conditions normally will not be released; photographing graves/temporary cemeteries is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPSEC and privacy accountability for VI
rubrics_metrics.description: All personnel are accountable for adherence to OPSEC and privacy regulations in the acquisition, distribution, and use of personal video, audio, and photographic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving VI in Defense imagery system
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PA product meets the VI definition in DoDI 5040.02 then DoD policy mandates that strategic, operational, tactical, and joint interest imagery will be centrally received, managed, and distributed as a shared asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA offices will coordinate and facilitate flow of VI to the Defense Imagery Management Operations Center through the Defense Visual Information Distribution Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with DA Pam 25-91 for VI documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs must comply with provisions of DA Pam 25-91 concerning usage of Defense VI activity numbers and the disposition of VI documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCPA approval for VI products intended for public release
rubrics_metrics.description: VI products made by the Army and intended primarily for public release (excluding materials to be used locally or dealing with spot news events that occur without prior planning or knowledge) must be approved by OCPA prior to committing military funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See DA Pam 25-91 for policies on producing VI products and AR 601-208 for Army branding guidance for externally released materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of commercial/copyrighted AV products
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders may use commercial and copyrighted audio and visual products if all fees have been paid and all rights to use the product have been obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must consult with their PAO, servicing SJA, and printing control officer, when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes for Army exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits (displays, models, devices, materials at conventions, conferences, exhibits, fairs, or on military installations) primarily serve to support recruiting and retention efforts or further Army professional, scientific, and technical interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and approvals for Army exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits at international trade shows are governed by 10 USC 113 and require Secretary of Defense determination; senior commanders may approve exhibit participation at local events; exhibits may be displayed where the general public gathers provided they are not used specifically to draw the public to that location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA units will request approval and coordinate with OCPA when national/international media could cover participation, forwarding intent at least 60 days prior to event. The period authorized for exhibits is normally the duration of the event; indemnity insurance normally required only for certain exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pentagon exhibit requirements and request data
rubrics_metrics.description: Armed Forces exhibits displayed on the Pentagon concourse must conform to regulation: no classified material; maximum permissible weight 150 pounds per square foot; proposals from commercial concerns limited to items in military inventory or service-testing program; references to commercial concerns limited to a 4-by-6 inch plaque or credit line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests forwarded to OCPA for ATSD (PA) approval at least 40 calendar days before desired display period must contain size of area, time desired, alternate dates, contact info, special electrical requirements, title and brief description (including sound volume control), statement security review made or accompanying material if not cleared, and statement that display will contain no commercial references beyond allowed plaque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lending, leasing, and donation policy references
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on lending or leasing materiel and facilities follow other ARs: AR 700-131 (lending/leasing), AR 725-1 (lending property to veterans/scouting), AR 840-10 (lending/selling/donating flags), AR 840-1 (DA Seal/DA Plaque), AR 405-80 (private persons using Army real estate), AR 700-131 and AR 735-5 (lending property to other government agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explosives and pyrotechnics participation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation of Army personnel in public events involving use of explosives is generally not advisable; units may approve participation only when it meets established safety criteria, a risk assessment has been performed and accepted at the appropriate level per DA Pam 385-30, and participation is clearly in the interest of the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using explosives on military installations at discretion of ACOMs; using antique weapons not routinely fired is prohibited; restrictions do not apply to routine salutes authorized in AR 600-25; local commanders may approve rifle and cannon salutes conducted off-post as part of an approved PA program if safety/risk assessment done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donation of obsolete or condemned combat equipment eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 10 USC 2572, certain organizations are authorized to acquire obsolete or condemned combat equipment for public display or ceremonial purposes (municipal corporations; Soldiers’ Monument associations; state museums; incorporated educational museums; local posts of veterans associations; recognized foreign war veterans associations; local or national units of foreign war veterans recognized by their government).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See AR 870-20 for details about the loan program.
